title: NCPatcher project configuration
description: Schema for ncpatcher.yaml (configuration version 2). The older ncpatcher.json is a different schema and is not described here; run `ncpatcher migrate` to convert it.

version.description: Configuration schema version. 2 is the YAML schema; a file with no version key is read as the v1 JSON schema.

vars.description: Named values usable as ${vars.NAME} anywhere in this file. Resolved lazily, so declaration order does not matter, and overridable with --var NAME=VALUE.

prefix.description: Cross-toolchain prefix, e.g. arm-none-eabi-. Overridable with --toolchain or NCPATCHER_TOOLCHAIN.

threads.description: Compile jobs to run at once. 0 means one per hardware thread. Overridable with -j or NCPATCHER_JOBS.

hooks.description: Named commands run before or after the build. Cannot be combined with the compatibility pre-build/post-build keys.

files.description: Loose files copied into NitroFS after pre-build hooks and before compilation. Each key is the '/'-separated path in the ROM. A string value is the source path, relative to the project. A mapping value carries the source plus options: `id` claims an existing file id and renames it to this path, which keeps every other id where it is instead of appending a new one at the end of the table. Missing destinations may only be created under z_new/, unless `id` names a file that already exists. An entry here overrides anything `file-trees` swept to the same destination. A key may also name a file inside a Nitro archive, as `ARCHIVE/menu_title.narc!menu/title/USA/vs.bmg`, which is the archive's ROM path, `!`, then the path within it. The archive must already exist and must already hold that member: archives are edited in place, never added to, because game code reads a member by its file id and inserting one renumbers every member after it. `id` cannot be combined with an archive destination, since it renames a loose file.

oneOf.description: The source path, relative to the project.

source.description: The source path, relative to the project.

id.description: An existing file id to claim. The file keeps this number and is renamed to this entry's path, so nothing after it is renumbered. The id must already exist and must live in the destination's parent directory.

file-trees.description: Directories swept wholesale into NitroFS, so that adding a file to the ROM is adding a file on disk rather than editing a list. Modules declare their own with `nitrofs` in module.yaml; these are the project's. A directory whose name ends in `_narc` means the Nitro archive beside it: `ARCHIVE/menu_title_narc/menu/title/USA/vs.bmg` replaces that member inside `ARCHIVE/menu_title.narc`. Only the outermost such directory is read that way. A ROM that genuinely holds a directory named `*_narc` has to be written in `files:` instead, where no convention applies.

dir.description: The source directory, relative to the project.

layered.description: Read the first path segment under `dir` as a variant name rather than part of the ROM path, so only the built variant's subtree applies. A variant with no directory contributes nothing rather than failing.

base-variant.description: A layer applied underneath the built variant, so the common case is written once and a variant only states its differences. Requires `layered`.

into.description: A ROM path prefix for everything the tree produces. Default is the ROM root.

files-dump.description: Where to write the ROM's file table as `ncpatcher.files/1` JSON (schema/files.schema.json), after NitroFS insertion and before the post-files hooks. `${ncp.fileDump}` expands to its absolute path, so a hook that turns file ids into constants can be handed it. A top-level key rather than `files.dump`, because `files:` is a mapping of ROM paths and a ROM may perfectly well contain a file called `dump`.

files-reserve.description: A '/'-separated z_new/ path created as an empty placeholder before any other file the build adds, so that it is given the first new file id and nothing loadable is. Some games hold arrays of file ids in compiled code, terminated by a sentinel that is the id one past the last file the retail ROM shipped with, which is exactly the id the first added file would otherwise get. Whether a game does this, and which id it is, is a fact about the game rather than about NitroFS, so nothing is reserved unless this names it. New Super Mario Bros. needs `z_new/reserved`, which is what `init --template nsmb` writes. The path may not also appear in `files:` or be supplied by a `file-trees:` entry: the placeholder has to stay empty.

variants.description: Named define/file matrices selected by `build --variant NAME`; `build --all-variants` builds every entry in declaration order.

pre-build.description: Compatibility spelling for unnamed pre-build hooks.

post-build.description: Compatibility spelling for unnamed post-build hooks.

targets.description: The ARM binaries this project compiles code into. Optional: a project that only replaces assets patches no code and declares no targets.

address.description: A 32-bit address. Either a number or a string, so that 0x-prefixed hex reads as it does in a disassembler.

stringList.description: A list that appends to whatever the level above contributed. The mapping form replaces or subtracts instead.

set.description: Replaces everything inherited. An empty list means nothing.

name.description: Human-readable name shown in build output and failures.

run.description: Command passed to the platform command runner. ${...} references are expanded before it runs.

cwd.description: Child working directory, relative to the project root by default.

env.description: Environment variables added to or overriding the child environment.

when.description: Build phase that runs the hook. post-files runs after NitroFS insertion and before compilation, which is the only point where a generator can see the file ids this build assigned and still have its output compiled.

defines.description: Preprocessor definitions added for this variant. Command-line -D definitions still come last.

files.description: NitroFS source overrides and additions for this variant, merged by destination path with the project files mapping. Accepts the same string or {source, id} forms as `files`.

banner.description: Overrides `rom.banner` for this variant. Same rule: it must be exactly as long as the ROM's own banner.

module-variants.description: Which layer of a module's `nitrofs` tree this variant selects, for modules that do not name their layers the way this project names its variants — a module split by region where the project splits by language, or one saying `french` where the project says `fr`. Keys are module names, values are the module's own layer name. Without a mapping the variant's own name is used, and a module that has no such layer contributes nothing. A layer named here must exist: naming it is an assertion, so a typo is an error rather than a silent fallback to the module's base layer.

flags.description: Compiler and linker flags. common reaches all three compilers; defines reach the assembler too, since assembly is compiled through -x assembler-with-cpp.

dir.description: Directory holding the extracted ROM: arm9.bin, arm7.bin, the overlay tables and the overlay binaries. Mutually exclusive with file.

file.description: A .nds read and written directly, as opposed to an extracted directory. Mutually exclusive with dir.

output.description: Where to write the patched ROM. Omit to patch rom.file in place. Only meaningful alongside rom.file.

backup.description: Directory holding pristine copies of every binary the patcher touches. `ncpatcher restore` puts them back.

banner.description: A replacement icon/title banner, as a project-relative path. Not part of `files:`: the banner is a region of its own that the header points at rather than a NitroFS file, so no ROM path would name it. The replacement must be exactly as long as the ROM's own banner: its length is fixed by the version it declares, so a different length is a different format rather than a bigger banner, and the build refuses rather than laying the container out again around it. A variant may override it, though one banner normally serves every build: the region carries a title in all six console languages at once.

layout.description: Naming convention of the extracted ROM directory. A preset name, or a mapping of file names, optionally with `preset:` naming the one to start from.

arm9-slack.description: Spare room to leave after arm9 when a .nds has to be laid out again, so that later builds fit in place. `auto` lets ncpatcher choose.

build.description: Directory for object files, the linker script, the ELF and the log. Relative to the project directory.

workdir.description: Base directory that this target's includes and sources are resolved against. Defaults to the directory the configuration file is in.

arena-lo.description: Address of the arena low pointer, which appended code is placed above.

symbols.description: Linker script naming the addresses of the game's own functions.

region-catalog.description: Path to a file listing the overlays this game has and how large each may grow. Shared game knowledge, so it usually lives outside the project. Entries nothing lands in are dropped, and the target's own regions override what it says.

dest.description: Where this region's code goes: `main` for the ARM binary itself, or `ovNN` for overlay NN.

mode.description: append adds code after the existing binary; replace overwrites it; create makes a new overlay.

maxsize.description: Refuses to build if the region grows past this. Worth setting for an overlay that has something after it in memory.

sources.description: Glob patterns, matched against the target's workdir. Supports *, ?, [abc], {a,b}, ** as a whole segment, and !pattern to exclude.

overwrites.description: Address ranges of the original binary this region is allowed to write over, as [start, end] pairs.

modules.description: Feature modules the project enables, each a directory with a module.yaml.

dir.description: Directory holding one subdirectory per module.

dump.description: Where to write the resolved module graph as JSON, before the pre-build commands run.

oneOf.description: A module directory name, enabled with nothing overridden.

optional.description: The module may be absent. Without this a missing module is an error.

target.description: Move the component to this processor or overlay. Refused, with a warning, when the module locked its target with a leading '!'.

defines.description: New values for defines the component already declares.
